about.title: Context and rationale
about.lead: Through original analyses and case studies conducted in several Francophone countries, the report highlights the main obstacles to accessing international finance and puts forward concrete recommendations to simplify procedures, strengthen national capacities and better respond to countries' priorities.
about.p1: Developing countries face a dual emergency: accelerating climate action and halting biodiversity loss while pursuing their sustainable development goals. At the same time, the financing landscape has become more complex and fragmented, with multiple bilateral donors, multilateral institutions, vertical funds and new instruments (green bonds, debt-for-nature swaps, carbon markets, etc.) coexisting.
about.p2: The joint OECD-OIF/IFDD report “Access to climate and biodiversity finance, from global commitments to country action” provides unprecedented empirical insight into how climate and biodiversity finance is allocated, the determinants of this access (needs, merit, donor interests, language, etc.), and the obstacles countries face, particularly Francophone ones.
about.p3: As the Decade of Action for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) draws to a close, and in the context of the climate and biodiversity agendas, the High-Level Political Forum (HLPF) offers a strategic platform to debate the conditions for better access to finance, from the perspective of both recipient countries and donors. The side event will mark the official launch of the joint report at United Nations Headquarters, and provide a space for political and technical dialogue on the reforms to be pursued by donors, countries and the multilateral system.
about.caseStudies: Case studies: Armenia, Gabon, Madagascar, Saint Lucia, Senegal, Togo

item1.title: Present the report
item1.text: Present the key findings and recommendations of the OECD-OIF/IFDD report on access to climate and biodiversity finance.

item2.title: High-level dialogue
item2.text: Give the floor to high-level decision-makers on the reforms needed to make finance more accessible, predictable and aligned with national priorities.

item3.title: Country experiences
item3.text: Highlight country experiences, particularly from Francophone countries: national financing strategies, accreditation, donor coordination, private sector mobilisation and financial innovation.

item4.title: Operational dialogue
item4.text: Foster an operational dialogue between countries, donors, vertical funds and multilateral development banks: simplified procedures, harmonised requirements, capacity support, language barriers.

speakers.title: High-level speakers
speakers.subtitle: Decision-makers and experts gathered for the official launch of the report at UN Headquarters.
speakers.lead: A high-level dialogue will bring together governments, donors, international funds and development partners to discuss the reforms needed to accelerate the implementation of the climate, biodiversity and sustainable development goals.

programme.title: Format and agenda
programme.subtitle: 90 minutes with simultaneous English / French interpretation.

item1.title: Welcome and introduction
item1.text: Setting the HLPF context and the link between the SDGs and the climate / biodiversity agendas. By Mr Michel Xavier Biang (OIF) or Mr Thomas Schnoell (OECD).

item2.title: Technical presentation of the OECD-OIF/IFDD report
item2.text: Analysis of climate and biodiversity finance flows, allocation model results and implications for countries' access (Mr Juan Casado-Asensio, OECD). Country case study findings: national strategies, governance, accreditation, donor coordination, financial innovation and language barriers (Mr Tounao Kiri, IFDD-OIF).

item3.title: High-level panel
item3.text: Guided discussion around 2-3 central questions: how to structure an integrated national climate/biodiversity financing strategy? How to simplify access to funds? How to better coordinate donors? Moderated by an OIF/IFDD representative.

item4.title: Exchanges with the audience
item4.text: Questions and reactions from the audience, responses from panellists.

item5.title: Conclusion and way forward
item5.text: By Mr Michel Xavier Biang (OIF) or Mr Thomas Schnoell (OECD).

audience.title: Target audience
audience.item1: Ministerial and high-level representatives of developing countries, particularly Francophone ones
audience.item2: Representatives of bilateral donors (OECD DAC members)
audience.item3: Climate and biodiversity funds (GCF, GEF, Adaptation Fund, etc.)
audience.item4: Multilateral development banks and other international financial institutions
audience.item5: Civil society organisations, research institutes, etc.
